newsitem.title: USA: Clinton announces economic team, U.N. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton announces economic team, U.N. envoy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton announced on Friday he would nominate Rep. Bill Richardson as his next U.N. ambassador and would retain Robert Rubin as treasury secretary and Janet Reno as attorney general.

At a news conference detailing more key picks for his second-term administration, Clinton also said he had tapped Chicago-based lawyer William Daley to be commerce secretary, acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky to permanent status in that post and White House aide Gene Sperling to head the National Economic Council. All but Sperling require Senate confirmation.

"As president, I have worked to keep the American dream alive for all those who are willilng to work for it .... Today i am pleased to introduce most of the members of the (economic advisory) team that will build on our work," Clinton said. Other holdovers included Franklin Raines as head of the White House Office of Management and Budget, Lawrence Summers as Rubin's chief deputy at treasury and Carol Browner as head of the Environmental Protection Agency.

Richardson, 49, is a New Mexico Democrat who has built a formidable reputation as a globe-trotting diplomatic trouble-shooter with a knack for negotiating the release of Americans held prisoner or hostage abroad. At the United Nations he would succeed Madeleine Albright, whom Clinton has nominated to be his next secretary of state.

Rubin, 58, is a Clinton favourite and his renomination as treasury secretary was not in doubt. But Reno, also 58, had raised hackles among White House aides who did not consider her a team player, and her continuation in the Cabinet was unsure until a Thursday night meeting with Clinton.

Daley, 48, is part of a powerful Chicago political family that has produced two city mayors including the current one, his brother Richard. A lawyer and longtime Clinton political ally, Daley gave the gathering a start when he tumbled to the floor just after making acceptance comments and was helped from the room. He returned a few minutes later to applause.
Clinton also elevated Daniel Tarullo to the newly created post of Assistant to the president for International Economic Policy.

A former Harvard Law School professor who has worked in the departments of State, Justice and Commerce, Tarullo has labored in the shadows for nearly two years as the White House "sherpa" who prepares for Group of Seven (G7) economic summits.
